implementation_notes: Ruby's scope-exit hook is ensure, available on begin/rescue/else/ensure and on method and block bodies; it runs whether the block returned normally, raised, or was left through break/throw, and - as the syntax documentation states - it does not implicitly return the last evaluated statement, so a `return` inside ensure is a bug. Commit semantics are an explicit flag read by the ensure body, or an idempotent release; there is no guard object to construct, and ObjectSpace.define_finalizer is not a substitute because finalizers run at an arbitrary later time. The substitute for a guard that must run somewhere other than method exit is an explicit call or a block-taking method that yields inside the begin/ensure pair.
code_sketch:
def update(account, amount)
  tx = db.begin
  committed = false
  begin
    account.credit(amount)
    tx.commit
    committed = true
  ensure
    tx.rollback unless committed   # runs on raise, on return and on break
  end
end
pitfalls: A `return` inside an ensure block silently overrides the method's return value and discards a pending exception - the exit path must not transfer control.
ensure runs without access to the exception unless a rescue clause captured it, so cleanup that must react to the error has to rescue, act and re-raise.
An exception raised inside ensure replaces the original exception (the same trap as finally everywhere), so cleanup that can raise - IO during rollback - masks the real failure.
